newsitem.title: USA: JFK imports 214,097 cartons of tomatoes in January 1997.
newsitem.headline: JFK imports 214,097 cartons of tomatoes in January 1997.

text.p: NEW YORK, March 5 (Renter) - More than 214,000 cartons of tomatoes were imported through cargo hubs at John F. Kennedy airport in January 1997.
George Jelinek of the USDA said 150,449 cartons originated in Spain and 63,648 cartons in Israel. In Jan last year combined imports from Sdpain and Israel were 145,236 cartons.

Industry sources at The United Farm Workers and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said the increase in imports last year could be attributed to the California floods and freezing conditions of Florida in early 1997.

Tomatoes, like other fruits and vegetables, are often shipped in cargo igloos with other perishables, so an actual metric tonnage on this cargo was not available when requested by Iberia Airlines. Iberia is the primary carrier for commodities oriqinating in Spain.
Cartons of tomatoes shipped from Israel and Spain into John F. Kennedy International airport during January 1996 and January 1997.
